description: When a veteran has disabilities affecting both a paired (bilateral) set of extremities or paired skeletal muscle groups, VA first combines only those bilateral disabilities together using the standard combined-ratings formula, then adds an extra 10% of that bilateral sub-combined value on top of it, BEFORE combining the result with the veteran's remaining (non-bilateral) disabilities and applying final rounding.
qualifying_pairs: Paired skeletal muscle groups (e.g. both hands, both feet, both knees, when rated separately)
non_qualifying_example: One arm + one leg does NOT qualify — the bilateral factor only applies to disabilities affecting the SAME paired body part type on both sides (e.g. left knee + right knee qualifies; left knee + right shoulder does not, since knee and shoulder are different paired-part categories)
calculation_note: Example structure: if bilateral disabilities combine to X%, the bilateral factor adds 0.1*X (rounded per VA convention) to X before that adjusted bilateral value re-enters the main combination sequence with the veteran's other (non-bilateral) disabilities, sorted by severity.
v1_scope: Implemented as an optional advanced checkbox in the combined-rating calculator ("Do any of these disabilities affect paired left/right limbs?"), not required for the base calculator to function. Users with bilateral disabilities should be advised the tool provides an estimate and to confirm with an accredited VSO/attorney for claims involving bilateral factor.
